title: Loss-state representation invariance and nuisance inflation

objects.meaning: Declared future loss response that a loss state must preserve.
Surjective map from a richer raw representation to a base representation.
Partition by equality of the declared loss-response signature.
Extra raw coordinates do not alter the declared loss response.

results.claim: A surjective loss-faithful representation map induces a canonical bijection between the two loss-response quotient state spaces.
A richer loss signature factors through a surjective projection iff every projection fiber is loss-response homogeneous.
Raw simulator-state space can be inflated by an arbitrary 2^m nuisance factor while required loss-state complexity remains unchanged.
One hidden coordinate that changes the declared loss response breaks the proposed coarse projection by violating fiber homogeneity.

claim_ceiling: No recursive quotient-dynamics claim unless a separate lumpability/bisimulation closure is supplied.
No standalone novelty claim over sufficient-statistic, predictive-state, bisimulation, or lumpability theory.
open_extensions: Action-conditioned quotient dynamics under explicit lumpability/bisimulation conditions.
Cross-representation warning portability for joint warning/loss timing.
Empirical tests of whether measured state coordinates factor held-out loss endpoints.
